title: batchMint pre-approves nftMinter for type(uint256).max for the entire loop, exposing the full paymentAmount to the configured dispatcher
description: Allowance is set to `type(uint256).max` before the mint loop and revoked only after the loop completes (line 76, `forceApprove(nftMinter, 0)`). For the loop's duration the dispatcher (and any callback path it can trigger) has authority to pull the contract's full balance rather than just the metered per-mint `price`. The contract also explicitly omits a ReentrancyGuard, so any future callback path within a dispatcher widens the surface further.
impact: Latent. Allowance is set to 0 immediately after the loop, so no residual approval survives the call. During the loop the dispatcher could in principle pull the full `paymentAmount` in one go rather than the metered per-mint price. Today's BalancerPoolerV2 dispatcher does not exhibit this behavior; the surface is a defensive hardening recommendation rather than an exploitable bug. Caller's full `paymentAmount` is at risk only if a registered dispatcher later turns hostile, gains a callback bug, or invokes a token hook that re-enters.
attackPath: [Hypothetical] An owner registers a hostile dispatcher OR an existing dispatcher gains a callback path
Inside the loop, the dispatcher pulls the full type(uint256).max approval (capped by contract balance == paymentAmount) instead of just the metered per-mint price
Dispatcher returns success; subsequent mint iterations still succeed (or revert harmlessly); contract is drained of its prepayment with fewer than N NFTs delivered
recommendation: Replace the max approval with `paymentToken.forceApprove(address(nftMinter), paymentAmount)` (single-line change — bounds dispatcher authority by what the user already authorised). Optionally approve per-iteration with `nftMinter.getPrice(dispatcherIndex)` for an even tighter window. Update the L29 docstring claim about omitted reentrancy guards if the approach changes.
severityRationale: CONFIRM low. The cleanup `forceApprove(0)` on line 76 means no allowance survives the call, which substantially limits the surface. The remaining concern is intra-call dispatcher trust amplification — defensive hardening at best. Goes into the QA report with a one-line `forceApprove(paymentAmount)` recommendation.

classification.assumptions: Dispatcher trust model. The stated trust assumption in yield-claim-nft is that dispatchers are owner-vetted; this finding amplifies that surface for batch callers (full prepaid balance vs per-mint metered amount).
classification.externalRequirements: Hostile or buggy dispatcher; not currently the case.

scannerAttribution.dedupNotes: MERGED CODE-BNM-002 + ECON-003. Same root cause (max approval held across entire loop). CODE framed as drain authority by the dispatcher; ECON framed as reentrancy-callback surface combined with omitted nonReentrant. Both reach the same approve(paymentAmount) recommendation. Combined framing is stronger than either alone.

sanitization.notes: Not a known issue. Not in prior submissions. The yield-claim-NFT known-issue 'Owner trust assumptions for registering dispatchers' covers the dispatcher-trust angle in the yield-claim-NFT scope; in BatchNFTMinter the trust-amplification is a NEW surface (caller's full upfront balance vs. per-mint metered amount). Distinct from the parent owner-trust framing.
